ctwPassages.topic: How a warehouse shift manager uses a handoff log to brief the next shift

segments.text: A shift handoff log lets an outgoing warehouse manager brief the incoming crew without holding a meeting. Before

mentioned too, such as a forklift that stopped operating and now needs a technician before anyone can use it again. Customer requests appear in the same entry, like a pickup time confirmed for an early delivery set for the following morning. Anyone starting the new rotation can simply read these notes and start immediately instead of searching for someone with answers.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處應填 leaving，與句首的 Before 搭配構成「Before leaving」（離開之前），指外出的倉庫主管在下班離開前先做交接紀錄，符合上下文描述主管在離開崗位前列出待辦事項的情境。
此處應填 list，主詞 they（外出主管）需要一個動詞來說明他們「列出」哪些裝卸任務尚未完成，list 作動詞使用，後接 which loading tasks remain unfinished 作受詞子句，語意通順。
此處應填 loading，修飾 tasks，構成 loading tasks（裝卸貨任務），呼應段落主題為倉庫交接日誌，內容涉及尚未完成的裝卸作業，符合倉庫工作情境。
此處應填 remain，與 unfinished 搭配構成「remain unfinished」（仍未完成），說明這些裝卸任務的狀態尚未結束，符合前後文列出待辦事項的邏輯。
此處應填 so，作為連接詞表示「因此／以便」，連接前面「主管列出未完成任務」與後面「下一班可以立即接續」的因果關係，符合交接日誌的目的。
此處應填 next，修飾 team 構成「the next team」（下一班團隊），對應句首提到的 incoming crew（接手的班次），語意前後一致。
此處應填 can，作為情態助動詞，與後面的 continue 搭配構成「can continue」（能夠繼續），說明下一班團隊因看到交接紀錄而能夠立即接續工作。
此處應填 right，與後面的 away 搭配構成慣用語「right away」（立刻、馬上），強調下一班團隊可以毫不延遲地接續未完成的任務。
此處應填 Equipment，作為句子主詞，構成「Equipment trouble」（設備故障），承接段落內容從裝卸任務轉到另一類交接資訊——設備問題，如後文提到的堆高機故障。
此處應填 gets，與 mentioned 搭配構成被動語態「gets mentioned」（被提及），說明設備故障也是交接日誌中會記錄提及的內容之一，符合列舉交接事項的語境。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: A shift handoff log lets an outgoing warehouse manager brief the incoming crew without holding a meeting. Before leaving, they list which loading tasks remain unfinished so the next team can continue right away. Equipment trouble gets mentioned too, such as a forklift that stopped operating and now needs a technician before anyone can use it again. Customer requests appear in the same entry, like a pickup time confirmed for an early delivery set for the following morning. Anyone starting the new rotation can simply read these notes and start immediately instead of searching for someone with answers.

ctwPassages.topic: How a fisheries biologist estimates a lake's fish habitat capacity

segments.text: A fisheries biologist visits a lake each autumn to estimate how many fish its habitat can support through winter. First,

larger predators. Next, crew members lower a weighted line at several spots across the water to check depth and locate cooler zones reached during warm afternoons. Oxygen readings and algae growth near the bottom further limit the remaining usable space once ice begins forming. Combining these measurements lets the team project a realistic capacity before conditions turn severe.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處指代前句主詞「A fisheries biologist」,由於主詞是單數但可能為任一性別,故用代名詞 they 來回指該生物學家,作為 record 的主詞,合乎上下文邏輯。
they record how much vegetation grows 為間接問句結構,how much 用來修飾 vegetation,表示「記錄植被生長的多寡」,是此子句必要的疑問詞。
vegetation 是 how much 所修飾的名詞,指「植被」,呼應後文 dense greenery(茂密的綠色植物),語意上與生物學家觀察湖岸植物生長情形一致。
along the shoreline 表示「沿著湖岸」,along 為介系詞,說明植被生長的位置分布在湖岸線上,符合描述生物學家觀察範圍的語境。
shoreline 指「湖岸線」,是 along 之後的受詞,說明植被生長的具體地點,並與後文 greenery(綠色植物)所在位置相呼應。
dense greenery 意指「茂密的綠色植物」,dense 形容植被的濃密程度,說明其足以提供幼魚躲藏空間,語意上與後文 offers...places to hide 相連貫。
dense greenery offers young trout places to hide 中,offers 為主詞 greenery 的動詞,表示「提供」躲藏之處,符合茂密植被具遮蔽功能的敘述邏輯。
trout(鱒魚)是此段主題「魚類棲地容量」中具體提及的魚種,young trout 指幼鱒魚,說明茂密植被為其提供躲避掠食者的場所。
places to hide 為不定詞片語修飾 places,表示「可供躲藏的地方」,to hide 說明該場所的功能用途,是此處文法上必要的不定詞結構。
hide from larger predators 表示「躲避體型較大的掠食者」,from 為介系詞,標示躲藏行為所欲迴避的對象,符合幼鱒魚利用植被自我保護的語境。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: A fisheries biologist visits a lake each autumn to estimate how many fish its habitat can support through winter. First, they record how much vegetation grows along the shoreline, since dense greenery offers young trout places to hide from larger predators. Next, crew members lower a weighted line at several spots across the water to check depth and locate cooler zones reached during warm afternoons. Oxygen readings and algae growth near the bottom further limit the remaining usable space once ice begins forming. Combining these measurements lets the team project a realistic capacity before conditions turn severe.

academic.title: When Small Manufacturers Bring Production In-House
academic.text:
Small manufacturers routinely decide whether to buy a component from an outside supplier or produce it themselves, a choice known as the make-or-buy decision. For low order volumes, buying is almost always cheaper: a supplier already owns the necessary tooling and machinery, and spreads that cost across many customers. As a company's own order volume rises, however, the calculation can shift. Producing a part in-house requires an upfront investment in tooling, molds, or specialized equipment, but once that investment is made, each additional unit costs comparatively little to produce. Beyond a certain volume threshold, the tooling cost is spread across enough units that in-house production becomes cheaper per unit than the supplier's price, even after including labor and materials.

Beyond cost, bringing production in-house often improves quality control. A company overseeing its own manufacturing process can adjust tolerances, catch defects earlier, and respond quickly to design changes, none of which is easily arranged through a supplier's separate operation. Some companies choose to insource even before the cost threshold is reached, judging that tighter oversight justifies a higher per-unit cost. Others wait until volume clearly exceeds the threshold, wary of tying up capital in equipment that a shift in demand could leave underused. Either way, the decision rests on comparing a fixed investment against variable savings accumulated over time.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why is buying a component from an outside supplier usually cheaper at low order volumes?

options.text: The supplier offers a lower price by using cheaper raw materials.
The supplier is legally required to charge below cost for new customers.
The supplier spreads tooling and machinery costs across many customers.

questions.explanationZh: 文中說明訂單量低時,供應商已擁有工具與機械,並將成本分攤給多位客戶,因此價格較低,與原料成本或法規要求無關。

questions.stem: The word "insource" in the passage is closest in meaning to

options.text: hire outside consultants to manage quality
sell a product to a new market
bring production in-house

questions.explanationZh: insource在文中指公司選擇將生產「移回廠內自製」,而非外包銷售新市場或聘請外部顧問管理品質。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that a company deciding to insource before the cost threshold is reached is most likely doing so because it

options.text: expects its order volume to permanently decline
values tighter quality control more than minimizing per-unit cost
has calculated that its supplier is overcharging for materials

questions.explanationZh: 文中指出即使尚未達到成本門檻,部分公司仍選擇自製,顯示他們更重視品質掌控,而非供應商定價過高或訂單量將永久下滑。

questions.stem: How does the second paragraph relate to the first?

options.text: It contradicts the cost-based reasoning presented in the first paragraph.
It introduces an additional, non-cost reason for the same decision discussed in the first paragraph.
It summarizes the entire passage before restating the make-or-buy decision.

questions.explanationZh: 第二段在第一段成本考量之外,補充品質控管這項另一項自製理由,而非反駁第一段論點或單純重述全文。

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the sentence beginning "Others wait until volume clearly exceeds the threshold"?

options.text: To describe a legal requirement companies must follow before insourcing.
To argue that most companies should never bring production in-house.
To illustrate a company that prioritizes avoiding underused equipment over early quality gains.

questions.explanationZh: 該句描述部分公司選擇等到訂單量明顯超過門檻,顯示他們寧可延後享有品質優勢,也要避免設備因需求變化而閒置,並非主張禁止自製或涉及法規。

ctwPassages.topic: How a small town plans its yearly music festival stage schedule

segments.text: Every year, a small town organizes the stage schedule for its music festival. Organizers

. Bigger acts then perform later once evening crowds gather and fill the entire park. Food vendors carefully plan their serving hours around that posted timetable. They expect that hungry visitors will buy more snacks whenever lines stay short. This steady approach keeps everyone ready for opening day.

gaps.explanationZh: 主詞為 Organizers（複數），此句描述例行性安排，須用現在式動詞 select，語意為「挑選演出時段」，與後文 performance times 搭配。
select 之後需接受詞，performance times 指「演出時段」，與下一句 several weeks before the event begins 的時間規劃語境呼應。
several 後須接複數名詞表示期間長度，weeks（週）符合「活動開始前數週」規劃時程的語意。
event 為前文已提及的特定音樂節活動，故需用定冠詞 the 表示特指，而非泛指的一般活動。
主詞 the event 為單數第三人稱，現在式動詞須加 -s，begins 表示活動「開始」，與 before 搭配表時間先後。
Local 為形容詞需修飾名詞，bands（樂團）為本句主詞，且與後文 Bigger acts 形成對比，指本地樂團與大牌演出者的差異。
主詞 bands 為複數，現在式動詞不加 -s，receive（獲得）符合「樂團獲得時段」的語意，並與 typically 的例行語氣一致。
afternoon（下午）修飾 slots，與後句 evening crowds 形成時間對比，說明本地樂團排在較早的下午時段演出。
slots 與 lineup 之間須用介系詞 in 表示「在陣容/節目表之中的時段」，符合英文慣用搭配 in the lineup。
lineup（節目陣容、演出名單）為介系詞 in the 之後的名詞，指音樂節整體的演出排程表，與全文討論 stage schedule 的主題一致。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Every year, a small town organizes the stage schedule for its music festival. Organizers select performance times several weeks before the event begins. Local bands typically receive early afternoon slots in the lineup. Bigger acts then perform later once evening crowds gather and fill the entire park. Food vendors carefully plan their serving hours around that posted timetable. They expect that hungry visitors will buy more snacks whenever lines stay short. This steady approach keeps everyone ready for opening day.

academic.title: How Earthworm Tunnels Help Garden Soil
academic.text:
Earthworms constantly dig narrow tunnels as they move through garden soil. These tunnels do more than let the worms travel. They also create small channels that air can pass through, reaching plant roots that would otherwise struggle to get enough oxygen. Loose, tunneled soil lets rainwater soak in rather than run off the surface, so roots receive water more evenly after a storm.

As earthworms eat their way through soil, they also produce castings, a nutrient-rich waste material left behind in their tunnels. These castings contain nitrogen, phosphorus, and other nutrients that plants need to grow strong. Over time, a garden with many earthworms often has darker, richer soil than one without them, because the castings build up close to where roots can reach them.

Gardeners sometimes measure earthworm activity by counting tunnel openings on the surface after rain. A high number usually means healthy, well-aerated soil underneath. Because of this simple sign, some gardeners treat earthworms as a rough indicator of overall soil health, checking for their tunnels before testing soil in more expensive ways.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what do earthworm tunnels allow air to do?

options.text: Mix with rainwater before it evaporates
Reach plant roots more easily
Escape from the soil surface completely

questions.explanationZh: 文中說明蚯蚓形成的通道能讓空氣到達植物根部,並非讓空氣完全逸出土壤表面或與雨水混合後蒸發。

questions.stem: The word "castings" in the passage most nearly means

options.text: waste material left behind by earthworms
seeds planted by gardeners
small tools used for digging

questions.explanationZh: castings指蚯蚓消化後留下的排泄物,富含養分,並非挖土工具或園丁播下的種子。

questions.stem: It can be inferred that a garden with very few tunnel openings after rain probably has

options.text: soil that is too rich in nutrients
fewer earthworms and less aerated soil
roots that grow unusually deep

questions.explanationZh: 文中指出蚯蚓通道數量多代表土壤通氣良好,因此雨後通道開口很少,合理推論代表蚯蚓數量少、土壤通氣較差。

questions.stem: How does the second paragraph build on the first?

options.text: It repeats the same point about rainwater absorption.
It disproves the claim made about tunnels in the first paragraph.
It adds a second way earthworms improve soil, beyond creating air channels.

questions.explanationZh: 第二段在第一段的通氣效果之外,補充蚯蚓排泄物提供養分這項改善土壤的另一方式,並未推翻或單純重複第一段內容。

questions.stem: Why does the passage mention that gardeners count tunnel openings after rain?

options.text: To explain a simple way gardeners estimate soil health
To show that tunnel counting is more accurate than any lab test
To argue that gardeners should avoid watering their soil

questions.explanationZh: 文中提到園丁藉由雨後計算通道開口數量,簡單判斷土壤健康狀況,並非主張此方法比實驗室檢測更準確或建議避免澆水。

ctwPassages.topic: How occupational health clinics use recovery-pacing plans to return patients to full activity

segments.text: Occupational health clinics often rely on a recovery-pacing plan to guide an injured worker safely back toward full activity. Clinicians

to the discomfort a patient reports during each session, not according to a fixed calendar. Subsequent visits then track whether fatigue is trending downward across consecutive appointments, confirming that the regimen remains appropriate. Only once this evidence accumulates consistently does a provider authorize a complete, unrestricted return to ordinary duties.

gaps.explanationZh: 主詞為複數的 Clinicians，且全句用現在式描述臨床常規做法，故動詞須用原形 raise（提高），與後面受詞 exertion levels 搭配，指「提高所指派的運動強度」。
assigned 為過去分詞作形容詞，修飾 exertion levels，表示「（先前）被指派的」運動強度等級，語意上與病人被分配到的訓練強度相符。
levels 是動詞 raise 的受詞，與前面的 exertion 組成複合名詞 exertion levels（運動強度等級），指臨床人員調整的對象。
careful 為形容詞，與後面並列的 incremental 一起修飾 stages，表示調整是「謹慎且漸進的」階段，呼應全文強調循序漸進、而非一次到位的核心概念。
stages 為名詞，作介系詞 in 的受詞，與 careful, incremental 兩個形容詞搭配，指「謹慎漸進的階段」，說明強度提升是分階段進行的。
than 與前面的 rather 構成固定搭配 rather than（而非），用以對比「分階段漸進」與「一次全部調整」兩種做法，凸顯文章強調前者。
at 與 all... once 構成固定片語 all at once（一次全部），在此表示與漸進方式相對立的做法，符合 rather than all at once 的語意。
Exercise 為名詞，與 intensity 組成複合名詞 Exercise intensity（運動強度），作為該句主詞，句首字母須大寫。
主詞 Exercise intensity 為單數（不可數概念視為單一整體），故 be 動詞須用 is，與被動語態 is adjusted（被調整）搭配。
according 與後面的 to 構成固定片語 according to（根據），表示強度調整的依據是病人回報的不適程度，而非固定行事曆。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Occupational health clinics often rely on a recovery-pacing plan to guide an injured worker safely back toward full activity. Clinicians raise the assigned exertion levels in careful, incremental stages rather than all at once. Exercise intensity is adjusted according to the discomfort a patient reports during each session, not according to a fixed calendar. Subsequent visits then track whether fatigue is trending downward across consecutive appointments, confirming that the regimen remains appropriate. Only once this evidence accumulates consistently does a provider authorize a complete, unrestricted return to ordinary duties.

academic.title: How a Postal Reform Changed Everyday Correspondence
academic.text:
In the mid-nineteenth century, a sweeping reform of postal rates transformed how ordinary people communicated across long distances. Before the reform, the cost of sending a letter depended on the number of sheets enclosed and the distance it traveled, a system so expensive that many households reserved letter-writing for urgent or infrequent occasions. The reform replaced this variable pricing with a single, low, prepaid rate regardless of distance, provided the letter fell under a modest weight limit.

The immediate effect was a sharp rise in personal correspondence. Families separated by migration or employment began exchanging letters far more frequently, no longer weighing every page against its cost. Historians studying postal records from the period have noted that letter volume in some regions multiplied several times over within a decade of the reform, a pace too rapid to attribute to population growth alone.

The reform's influence extended beyond personal letters. Shopkeepers, who had previously relied on in-person visits or costly couriers to manage accounts with distant suppliers, began keeping more of their routine business correspondence by mail, since even frequent, brief notes remained affordable under the new flat rate. This shift left a denser paper trail than earlier record-keeping practices had produced, one that historians now treat as unusually rich evidence of ordinary commercial life in the period, rather than merely a footnote to postal history.
